title: Are Black Friday Deals Actually Real?
description:
A price tracker found that a third of last season's Black Friday deals had been cheaper earlier, and JCPenney once raised prices just so it could mark them down.
#blackfriday #shopping #money #shorts

Sources: Visualping Black Friday 2025 fake deals report; ConsumerAffairs (Nov 2, 2026); MobileSyrup (Dec 4, 2025); AP via MPR News (Apr 8, 2013); Chief Executive (2013); Reuters via Coupons in the News (Mar 2013); Benzinga, citing the New York Post (Mar 2013)
Photos: paul bica, Stein Magne, Jessie Pearl, JeepersMedia, danxoneil (CC BY 2.0, Flickr)
first_comment: Be honest: ever bought something just because the tag said "50% off"? Yes or no? 🏷️

scenes.say: One in three Black Friday deals isn't a deal at all.
scenes.source: Visualping Black Friday 2025 report ('one-third of Black Friday/Cyber Monday deals offered no real savings'); ConsumerAffairs Nov 2 2026 (roughly one-third had been available for less earlier); MobileSyrup Dec 4 2025

scenes.say: A price tracker watched {2,600|twenty six hundred} products every day last season.
scenes.source: Visualping report (2,620 products, nine retailers, daily checks Oct 1 to Dec 1 2025); ConsumerAffairs ('more than 2,600 products')

scenes.say: The fakes still cost {37%|thirty seven percent} more than their lowest price of the season.

visual.title: Fake deal vs. its lowest price

scenes.source: Visualping ('still 37% higher than the product's lowest observed price', average); ConsumerAffairs ('37% higher'); MobileSyrup ('still 37 per cent higher')

scenes.say: For luggage? {61%|sixty one percent} of the deals.
scenes.source: Visualping (luggage 61%, highest share of fake deals); ConsumerAffairs (luggage 61%); MobileSyrup (luggage 61%)

scenes.say: The crossed-out price is only there to make the real one feel tiny.
When JCPenney dropped fake sales in {2012|twenty twelve}, revenue fell {25%|twenty five percent}.
scenes.source: AP via MPR News Apr 8 2013 ('Penney ditched coupons and most of its sales events in favor of everyday low prices'; 'Revenue fell 25 percent, to $12.98 billion, from the previous year's $17.26 billion'); Chief Executive 2013 ('fair and square' pricing replacing 'fake prices'; sales plunged from ~$17.5B to $13B)

scenes.say: So Penney raised prices, just to mark them down again.
scenes.source: Reuters via Coupons in the News Mar 27 2013 ('has begun raising the regular prices on much of its merchandise'); Benzinga citing NY Post Mar 2013 ('marking up its prices so that they can subsequently be discounted')

scenes.say: So skip the crossed-out price and check the price history. Because
